basis: Bilateral duplication of the thumb is a congenital skeletal malformation.
Acute leukemia of megakaryocytic lineage arising in blood and bone marrow.
Inherited disorders of erythropoiesis with sideroblasts and anemia; syndromic manifestations and iron-related organ damage are not universal across this umbrella.
Benign grade I tumor arising in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Colorectal adenomatous polyposis defines disease; gastric and duodenal polyps share this axis. Retinal pigment hypertrophy generally does not impair vision; other tumors are separate risks.
Developmental impairment of speech-sound production is a neurodevelopmental communication disorder.

Congenital microcephaly with brain malformations; adducted thumbs 11/12 and knee contracture 1/2 support skeletal involvement; glaucoma 1/2 supports ocular involvement. Pigment macules are non-damaging.
B-cell immunodeficiency and cardiomyopathy define syndrome; neutropenia occurs in 2/3. Bronchiectasis is a separate secondary disease; neurologic/myopathic findings are not consistently attributable.
Cyclic eosinophilia with immune-mediated subcutaneous angioedema defines the syndrome; transient episodes do not establish additional visceral organ damage.
Loss of peripheral peroneal nerve function; resulting weakness does not establish a separate primary muscle disorder.
Intellectual disability and objective myopathy define syndrome; dental caries with palatal abnormalities occurs in 30-79%, supporting oral involvement. Ocular abnormalities are occasional.
Toxic injury to the brain or other nervous system structures defines this umbrella; additional organ damage depends on the specific toxin.
Familial infantile epilepsy is defined by recurrent cerebral seizures.
Progressive cerebellar and peripheral nerve degeneration; scoliosis, pes cavus and distal amyotrophy occur in 30-79%. Abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Isolated inherited myocardial disease with ventricular dilatation and common heart failure.
Benign bone-forming neoplasm arising in skeletal bone.
Inherited pure red-cell aplasia defines Diamond-Blackfan anemia; no common additional organ damage is established for this subtype.
Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia defines the disorder; isolated mucopolysacchariduria does not establish a metabolic disease.
Defined as a benign adipocytic tumor of lumbosacral vertebral tissue; spinal cord origin or common neural injury is not established.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the renal pelvis.
Primary lung adenocarcinoma with papillary architecture.
Benign epithelial neoplasm of the skin.
Rickettsia prowazekii infects vascular endothelium and causes systemic small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash and acute confusion do not establish lasting skin or brain damage.
Umbrella for diseases of the ocular lens; systemic manifestations of individual subtypes do not apply across the group.
Hair abnormalities, cholestasis and neurodevelopmental disease define THNS; hip dysplasia 3/3 and dislocation 2/3 support skeletal involvement. Ptosis 4/4 and PDA 2/4 omitted at cap.
